annotations.description: Keeping a 7-card hand with 4 Islands, no red sources, and only 3 spells in what appears to be a UR deck. While the blue cards form a functional curve (Lofty Denial turn 2, Pretender turn 3, Ghostlight turn 5), the hand is land-heavy and missing half the deck's color, meaning any red cards drawn will be dead until a red source appears.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept the 7-card hand with 4 Islands and no red mana sources.
annotations.betterLine: Mulligan to 6 to look for a more balanced hand with both colors represented and a better land-to-spell ratio.

annotations.description: Nest Robber is a 2/1 with haste, and the opponent has no creatures on the battlefield — only two Islands. There is zero risk in attacking for 2 damage. The player declined to attack into an empty board, giving up free damage. Over the course of the game, 2 damage can matter significantly, especially in an aggressive red deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Nest Robber into an empty board.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Nest Robber for 2 unblockable damage, bringing the opponent to 18.

annotations.description: Gem31P cast Bolt Hound into 2 open Islands with exactly 3 mana, leaving no ability to pay for Lofty Denial. The opponent countered Bolt Hound for free. With a Mountain still in hand, waiting one turn to play the 4th land would have allowed casting Bolt Hound with {1} open to pay through Lofty Denial.
annotations.actionTaken: Could not pay {1} for Lofty Denial because all lands were tapped after casting Bolt Hound, so it was countered.
annotations.betterLine: Wait one turn, play the 4th Mountain, then cast Bolt Hound with {1} open to pay for potential Lofty Denial. Could have cast Rummaging Goblin (also 3 mana) this turn instead as a less impactful spell to potentially bait the counter.

annotations.description: Nest Robber is a 2/1 with haste facing an Amoeboid Changeling that just entered (summoning sick) and the opponent has only 2 Islands tapped. The opponent has no untapped blockers and no mana available to cast anything. Attacking for 2 free damage is risk-free here — there's nothing the opponent can do to punish the attack. Missing 2 damage in an aggressive deck with burn spells matters for closing out the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Nest Robber.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Nest Robber for 2 uncontested damage, bringing the opponent to 18.

annotations.description: Nest Robber has a completely free attack here. Opponent's only untapped creature is Amoeboid Changeling (1/1), which would die to Nest Robber (2/1) without killing it. If unblocked, it deals 2 damage. Opponent is tapped out with no mana for tricks. There is zero downside to attacking with Nest Robber.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Nest Robber. It either deals 2 damage or kills Amoeboid Changeling for free (Nest Robber survives the block). Rummaging Goblin can stay back for its tap ability.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with 4 untapped Mountains and the opponent completely tapped out. At minimum, Rummaging Goblin could have been activated to filter the hand (discarding a less useful card to draw). Additionally, this was an ideal window to use Flame Lash or Fiery Conclusion on Warden of Evos Isle while the opponent couldn't counter it, preventing future cost-reduced flying threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without using any mana or abilities.
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, activate Rummaging Goblin to filter the hand. Strongly consider using Flame Lash on Warden of Evos Isle while the opponent is tapped out and can't counter it, or Fiery Conclusion (sacrificing the sick Weaselback Redcap) to kill Warden more efficiently.

annotations.description: Activating Amoeboid Changeling in postcombat main with no clear strategic benefit. None of the opponent's creatures have relevant creature types to remove, and granting types to own creatures doesn't accomplish anything this turn. This taps the Changeling unnecessarily, preventing it from being used next turn when it might be more relevant (e.g., during opponent's combat or when Bloodline Pretender enters).
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Amoeboid Changeling's tap ability with no apparent beneficial target or purpose.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn, keeping Amoeboid Changeling untapped as a potential blocker (even if small) and preserving its tap ability for a turn where it matters — such as after casting Bloodline Pretender to synergize with type manipulation, or during the opponent's turn to affect combat.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with the opponent completely tapped out (no mana to counter). Flame Lash could cleanly remove Warden of Evos Isle (a high-value cost-reduction creature for flying spells) with zero risk of countermagic. Additionally, Rummaging Goblin could have been activated to loot for free card selection.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without casting any spells or activating Rummaging Goblin.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Flame Lash targeting Warden of Evos Isle while the opponent is tapped out, preventing future discounted flying threats. At minimum, activate Rummaging Goblin to loot before passing.

annotations.description: MstMed Rookie timed out and didn't declare any attackers. Warden of Evos Isle is a 2/2 flyer facing no opposing flyers or reach creatures, meaning it attacks for 2 unblockable damage with zero risk. Missing this free damage is a clear waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Warden of Evos Isle for 2 unblockable flying damage. The Amoeboid Changeling could reasonably stay back for its tap ability.

annotations.description: Triple-blocking a 1/1 Amoeboid Changeling with all three available creatures (Nest Robber, Rummaging Goblin, and Weaselback Redcap). This is unnecessary overkill that exposes multiple creatures to potential combat tricks. Any single creature would suffice to block the 1/1.
annotations.actionTaken: Assigned all three creatures (Nest Robber, Rummaging Goblin, Weaselback Redcap) to block the 1/1 Amoeboid Changeling.
annotations.betterLine: Block with just Nest Robber (2/1 cleanly kills the 1/1) or Rummaging Goblin (1/1 trades), keeping other creatures safe from potential combat tricks. Rummaging Goblin is the best single blocker since it trades the least valuable creature.

annotations.description: Using Unsubstantiate to save a 1/1 Amoeboid Changeling from a bad block trades a flexible tempo/counter spell for a low-value creature. Unsubstantiate is more valuable as a pseudo-counterspell or for bouncing a bigger opposing threat later. The Changeling is only a 1/1 with modest utility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Unsubstantiate (likely targeting own Amoeboid Changeling) to save it from dying in combat.
annotations.betterLine: Let the Amoeboid Changeling die in combat and save Unsubstantiate for bouncing a more impactful opposing creature or countering a key spell. With Roaming Ghostlight already in hand for bounce effects, Unsubstantiate's flexibility as a pseudo-counterspell is more valuable than a 1/1 body.

annotations.description: Targeted Nest Robber (a cheap 2/1 haste creature easily replayed for 2 mana) with Unsubstantiate instead of Rummaging Goblin (a 3-mana value engine that provides repeatable card filtering). The Amoeboid Changeling dies regardless since it's blocked by three creatures, so the bounce should maximize tempo/value by removing the most impactful or expensive-to-replay creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Nest Robber (2-mana creature with no ongoing value) back to opponent's hand
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Rummaging Goblin back to opponent's hand - it costs 3 mana to replay, provides ongoing card advantage through its tap+discard ability, and is far more impactful to remove from the board.

annotations.description: Rummaging Goblin is blocking Amoeboid Changeling and will likely die in combat. Activating it before damage (tap + discard a card to draw a card) would provide free card filtering since the Goblin may not survive. This is essentially free value since the Goblin is going to die anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Rummaging Goblin before combat damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Rummaging Goblin (discarding the weakest card in hand, likely Nest Robber or Fiery Conclusion) to draw a fresh card before the Goblin potentially dies in combat.

annotations.description: Weaselback Redcap declined to attack when the opponent had no untapped creatures to block. This is free damage with zero risk. With 5 Mountains available, the Redcap could have been pumped twice to deal 5 damage, or at minimum dealt 1 damage for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on attacking, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Weaselback Redcap and pump it (e.g., twice for 5 damage, or once for 3 damage) to deal free damage to the opponent who is at 20 life. No blockers were available.

annotations.description: Used Flame Lash (4 damage to any target, including face) to kill a 2/2 Warden of Evos Isle when Volley Veteran could accomplish the same thing for the same mana cost while also developing a 4/2 body. Flame Lash is a premium burn spell that can target the opponent directly for lethal damage later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flame Lash to kill Warden of Evos Isle 2/2
annotations.betterLine: Cast Volley Veteran, which with Weaselback Redcap on board would deal 2 damage to Warden (killing it) while putting a 4/2 creature on the board, preserving Flame Lash for face damage or a bigger threat later.

annotations.description: Cast Bloodline Pretender (a 2/2 with limited upside) instead of playing Island first and casting Roaming Ghostlight (3/2 flyer that bounces opponent's Weaselback Redcap). Playing Island would give 6 mana, enough for Ghostlight's {3}{U}{U} cost. The flyer is a much stronger threat, and bouncing the opponent's only creature provides significant tempo. Bloodline Pretender could easily be cast next turn after playing the second Island.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bloodline Pretender for 3 mana without playing a land first
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, then cast Roaming Ghostlight targeting Weaselback Redcap with the bounce trigger. Cast Bloodline Pretender next turn.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Inniaz before playing the Island from hand. Inniaz is a 4/4 flyer but its key ability (triggering on 3+ flying attackers) is nearly impossible to activate with no other flyers on board. Roaming Ghostlight would provide a 3/2 flyer AND bounce the opponent's Volley Veteran 4/2 back to hand, which is likely more impactful. Additionally, the land should be played before casting spells for proper sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Inniaz, the Gale Force (which was rolled back due to mana payment issues)
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first, then cast Roaming Ghostlight targeting Volley Veteran to bounce it, getting a flyer on board while removing the opponent's biggest threat

annotations.description: With 3 creatures attacking into an empty board (no blockers), the player passed without using Weaselback Redcap's pump ability or Rush of Adrenaline, leaving 4 free damage on the table. Redcap's activation costs only mana (no card cost), and Rush of Adrenaline on an unblocked creature is guaranteed value with no risk of being blown out.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without pumping any attackers, dealing only 7 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Weaselback Redcap ({1}{R} for +2/+0) and cast Rush of Adrenaline on Redcap ({R} for +2/+1), using all 3 untapped Mountains to deal 11 damage instead of 7. At minimum, activate Redcap for free 2 extra damage.

annotations.description: Cast Rookie Mistake on opponent's already-tapped creatures, accomplishing nothing. Nest Robber getting -2/-0 doesn't matter since it's tapped and won't attack again until next turn (when the effect will have worn off). Volley Veteran getting +0/+2 is actively bad since it's an opponent's creature. This wastes a card for zero value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Rookie Mistake targeting Volley Veteran (+0/+2) and Nest Robber (-2/-0) while both are tapped, achieving nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, then cast Roaming Ghostlight to bounce Volley Veteran (the biggest threat) and establish a 3/2 flying blocker. Save Rookie Mistake for a combat where it would actually matter — shrinking an attacking creature and buffing a blocker.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Inniaz, the Gale Force instead of Roaming Ghostlight. Inniaz is just a 4/4 flyer here with no way to trigger its 3-flyer attack ability. Roaming Ghostlight would bounce the dangerous Volley Veteran 4/4 back to opponent's hand while also providing a 3/2 flying body — much better immediate board impact when at 12 life facing significant threats. Additionally, the mana plan failed (likely referencing a tapped land), wasting the action.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Inniaz, the Gale Force (which was rolled back due to mana payment failure)
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first for the land drop, then cast Roaming Ghostlight targeting Volley Veteran 4/4 to bounce the biggest threat and establish a flying blocker/attacker

annotations.description: Failed to cast Roaming Ghostlight due to an incorrect mana plan, effectively wasting the entire postcombat main phase. They had 5 untapped Islands available (enough for the 3UU cost) but the mana plan included a tapped Island. Additionally, they should have played their Island from hand first before attempting the cast to ensure maximum mana availability. Roaming Ghostlight bouncing the 4/4 Volley Veteran would have been an excellent defensive play at 12 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Roaming Ghostlight with an invalid mana plan that included a tapped Island, causing the game engine to roll back the action, resulting in nothing happening.
annotations.betterLine: Play the Island from hand first (land drop), then cast Roaming Ghostlight targeting the Volley Veteran 4/4, using the correct 5 untapped Islands for mana.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Weaselback Redcap's pump ability during combat when attacking unblocked. With 5 untapped Mountains, spending 2 on Redcap's +2/+0 would deal 9 instead of 7 damage (opponent to 3 instead of 5), while still leaving enough mana post-combat to play Mountain and cast Warcry Phoenix (4 mana from remaining 4 lands). The extra 2 damage is free in this scenario.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without pumping any attackers, dealing only 7 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Weaselback Redcap's ability ({1}{R}: +2/+0) to deal 9 damage total, bringing opponent to 3. Post-combat, play Mountain and cast Warcry Phoenix with remaining 4 mana.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with 5 untapped lands, a land drop available, and Warcry Phoenix castable. Opponent is at 5 life with no creatures. Deploying Warcry Phoenix (2/2 flying) alongside 3 existing creatures would create overwhelming pressure next turn. The unused land drop is pure value lost.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 5 unused mana, an unplayed Mountain, and Warcry Phoenix still in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain, then cast Warcry Phoenix (4 mana). This adds a flying threat to a board of 3 creatures against an opponent at 5 life with no blockers, likely setting up lethal next turn.

annotations.description: At 5 life facing lethal on board (7 power worth of creatures), the player attempted to cast Roaming Ghostlight without first playing an Island from hand. The mana payment failed and the cast was rolled back, wasting the priority window. With only 6 Islands and needing 5 mana, the player should have played the 7th Island first to ensure reliable mana payment. At 5 life, failing to deploy a blocker and bounce the Volley Veteran is potentially game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Roaming Ghostlight before playing a land, causing the mana payment to fail and the cast to be rolled back.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island from hand first (land drop), then cast Roaming Ghostlight targeting Volley Veteran to bounce the biggest threat and deploy a 3/2 flying blocker.

annotations.description: At 5 life facing three creatures (Nest Robber 2/1, Volley Veteran 4/2, Weaselback Redcap 1/1 that can pump), the player passed their postcombat main phase without playing a land or casting any spells. They had 6 untapped Islands, a land drop remaining, and Roaming Ghostlight (3UU) in hand which could bounce one of the opponent's creatures (most critically the Volley Veteran 4/2). They also had Inniaz, the Gale Force (3UU) as a 4/4 flying blocker. Playing an Island and casting Roaming Ghostlight to bounce Volley Veteran would dramatically reduce incoming damage next turn. Without any blocker or bounce, the opponent can attack for lethal (2+4+1 = 7, or even more with Weaselback pump, against 5 life).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase, ending the turn with no plays.
annotations.betterLine: Play an Island, then cast Roaming Ghostlight (3UU) targeting Volley Veteran to bounce the biggest threat. This leaves a 3/2 flying blocker and removes 4 power from the opponent's board, potentially surviving the next turn. Alternatively, cast Inniaz as a 4/4 flying blocker.
